text:
maya: hey folks, maya here (first day). trying to build the runtime from source on a Windows machine using WSL2 + docker. build goes through cmake/ninja but the final link fails with cublas/cudnn undefined refs. following the quickstart but hitting host/tooling mismatch i think. any onboarding tips?

maya: link snippet:

maya: ```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/src/kernels/cuda_kernels.o: in function `register_kernels':
undefined reference to `cublasGemmEx'
undefined reference to `cudnnConvolutionForward'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

maya: nvcc --version inside container: 12.1, but on host Windows drivers are 511.x via WSL2 GPU. I mounted /usr/local/cuda from host into container per a guide.

juan: welcome maya! :wave: first thing: avoid mounting random host CUDA bits into the container. WSL2 has its own driver surface and the container images we ship expect the toolkit to be inside the image or the VM, not a mixed mount. Run `ldd build/runtime | grep -E "cublas|cudnn|cuda"` inside the container to see unresolved libs.

rachel: +1. `libcublas` and `libcudnn` must be resolvable inside the build environment. If `ldd` says "not found" you either need the toolkit/cudnn installed in the image or to set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the right path. But on WSL mixing host and container libs often causes ABI issues.

samir: also check `file` on third_party .a files. If a static lib was built without PIC you can get weird relocation errors when linking to shared objects: try `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` or rebuild offending libs with `-fPIC`.

maya: ran `ldd` and I get `libcublas.so.12 => not found` and `libcudnn.so => not found`. I tried making symlinks from host /usr/local/cuda/lib64 into container but the binary crashes later.

juan: symlinks can hide deeper mismatches. Recommended options: 1) use the internal dev docker image `internal.redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-cudnn8` which contains matching toolkit + cuDNN, or 2) spin a linux VM (GCP/AWS) and install toolkit + cuDNN there. For WSL2, we don't officially support full GPU dev inside onboarding docs due to driver differences.

maya: ah — i'm on a personal laptop and hoped to avoid cloud. Is there a minimal list of packages to install so container works?

rachel: minimal steps (preferred order):
1) don't mount host CUDA into container.
2) use our dev image that already has CUDA+cuDNN. If you must build locally, install full CUDA toolkit (matching nvcc) and cuDNN into the machine under `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/targets/x86_64-linux/lib`, then run `sudo ldconfig`.
3) run `git submodule update --init --recursive` before cmake.
4) set cmake rpath: `-DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` so runtime finds libs without relying on env vars.

samir: also watch gcc version. CI/dev image uses gcc-11. Using gcc-12+ with nvcc sometimes causes compile-time or ABI oddness. If you get `ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_75' is not supported by this toolchain` adjust `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` to match your GPU, or set to `Auto` so PTX fallback is generated.

maya: i'm seeing a separate message earlier in logs: `relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against symbol ... can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC`. so i'll try the POSITION_INDEPENDENT option.

juan: yeah that explains some failures. run `file` on the offending .o/.a to confirm. If it's a third_party static archive, rebuild that submodule with `CFLAGS=-fPIC` or prefer shared libs.

infra-bot: infra-bot: Need a pre-provisioned GPU dev VM? Request `gpu-dev-onboard` in #eng-infra with your username and desired CUDA version. We maintain a ready image pinned to CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.9 + gcc-11 for onboarding.

maya: thanks. quick Q: what's the policy on using the distro package `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` vs official NVIDIA toolkit?

rachel: avoid distro `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` for dev — it often lags or uses different sonames. Use the official deb/tar from NVIDIA or our docker image. If you install via tarball, ensure `targets/x86_64-linux/lib` is present and run `sudo ldconfig` after placing cuDNN libs there.

samir: if you want to try quick debug without provisioning a VM: pull `internal.redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-cudnn8`, build inside it (no host mounts), and see if link succeeds. If that works, the issue is host/container mix.

maya: i'll try the internal image first. if that still fails i'll request an infra VM. appreciate the clear checklist. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:

dev-bot: dev-image-bot: docs: https://redwood.dev/dev-env. If onboarding, prefer `internal.redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-cudnn8-gcc11`. Ping #eng-infra for vm access.
